questions.stem: Explain why an adjacency list is more suitable for representing sparse graphs compared to an adjacency matrix.
markingGuide: Define sparse graphs as having relatively few edges.
State the space complexity of adjacency lists as $O(|V| + |E|)$.
State the space complexity of adjacency matrices as $O(|V|^2)$.
Explain that adjacency lists only store existing edges, reducing space usage.
questions.explanation: Sparse graphs have few edges. An adjacency list's space complexity is $O(|V| + |E|)$, which is lower than the $O(|V|^2)$ of an adjacency matrix. Adjacency lists only store existing edges, making them more space-efficient for sparse graphs.

questions.stem: Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of using adjacency matrices over adjacency lists for graph representation.
markingGuide: Advantage: Fast edge lookup with $O(1)$ time complexity.
Disadvantage: High space complexity of $O(|V|^2)$, inefficient for sparse graphs.
Advantage: Simple implementation and easy to understand.
questions.explanation: Adjacency matrices allow fast edge lookups in $O(1)$ time, are simple to implement, and easy to understand. However, they have a high space complexity of $O(|V|^2)$, making them inefficient for sparse graphs. Enumerating neighbours is slower, taking $O(|V|)$ time.
